title: Dimension functions restrict to strict localizations and are tested there
statement: Let $T$ be a Noetherian excellent scheme [def-exc-excellent-ring]. For a geometric point $\bar t$ above $t\in T$, let $\pi_{\bar t}:T_{(\bar t)}\to T$ be its strict localization [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. A dimension function on a scheme $S$ means a function $d:|S|\to\mathbf Z$ whose value decreases by one at every immediate geometric specialization: the reduced closure of the general point in the strict localization at the special geometric point has Krull dimension one [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. For every function $d:|T|\to\mathbf Z$, the function $d$ is a dimension function if and only if $d\circ|\pi_{\bar t}|$ is a dimension function on $T_{(\bar t)}$ for every geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$. In particular every dimension function on $T$ pulls back to a dimension function on each strict localization.

source.place: Expose XIV, Definition 2.1.8 and the following paragraph (etale restriction and locality), printed pp.211–212; strict-local version used at the start of the proof of Proposition 2.5.4, printed p.217.

proof.text: Fix $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ and put $L=T_{(\bar t)}$, $\pi=\pi_{\bar t}$. Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing $t$. The structural map $\pi$ factors through $U$: its inverse image contains the closed point of the local spectrum $L$, and an open containing that point is all of $L$ (a basic neighbourhood $D(g)$ of the maximal ideal has $g$ a unit). By [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-affine-chart-ind-etale], the coordinate ring of $L$ is ind-etale over $A$. Thus $\pi$ satisfies the local ind-etale hypothesis of [lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance]. By clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality], $L$ has a closed geometric lift $c:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to L$ with $\pi c=\bar t$.

source.place: Expose XIV, Definition 2.1.8 and following paragraph, printed pp.211–212; strict-local reduction in Proposition 2.5.4, printed p.217. Expanded using Stacks 04HX (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring), 05WR (lemma-quasi-finite-strict-henselization), and 0GIP (lemma-base-change-strict-henselization-quasi-finite).

proof.text: Suppose $d$ is a dimension function on $T$. Consider any immediate geometric specialization on $L$, with special geometric endpoint $b$ and a geometric general endpoint whose image is $v$ in $L_{(b)}$. Write $w$ for the underlying general point of $L$ and $z$ for its special point. The reduced closure of $v$ in $L_{(b)}$ has dimension one by hypothesis. Apply [lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance] to $\pi$ at $b$, using the same geometric field at $\pi b$. The canonical isomorphism $L_{(b)}\simeq T_{(\pi b)}$ is over $T$. It carries $v$ to a point over $\pi(w)$ and identifies their reduced closures, so the latter has dimension one as well. Being an isomorphism of local schemes it carries the closed point to the closed point, and by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality] the closed points of $L_{(b)}$ and $T_{(\pi b)}$ lie over $z$ and $\pi(z)$. Hence this point and the geometric point $\pi b$ witness an immediate geometric specialization on $T$. Therefore $d(\pi(z))=d(\pi(w))-1$. These are exactly the values of $d\circ|\pi|$ at $z,w$, proving that it is a dimension function on $L$.

source.place: Expose XIV, Definition 2.1.8 and following paragraph, printed pp.211–212; strict-local reduction in Proposition 2.5.4, printed p.217. proof.text: Conversely assume $d\circ|\pi_{\bar t}|$ is a dimension function for every $\bar t$. Take any immediate geometric specialization on $T$ with special endpoint $\bar t$ and general image $v$ in $L=T_{(\bar t)}$; by definition the reduced closure of $v$ in $L$ has dimension one. Let $c$ be the closed geometric lift of $\bar t$ supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality]. The closed-point iteration clause of [lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance], applied to $\pi$ at $c$ (so $\pi c=\bar t$), says that the canonical map $\varphi:L_{(c)}\to T_{(\bar t)}=L$ is an isomorphism over $T$: $\pi\circ\varphi=\pi\circ j$, where $j:L_{(c)}\to L$ is the structural map. Put $v'=\varphi^{-1}(v)$. Its reduced closure in $L_{(c)}$ is carried by $\varphi$ onto that of $v$, hence is one-dimensional, so $v'$ and $c$ give an immediate geometric specialization on $L$, with special point $j(\text{closed point})$, the closed point of $L$ by clause (1) of functoriality. The assumed dimension-function equation for $d\circ\pi$ on $L$ reads $d(\pi(\text{closed point of }L))=d(\pi(j(v')))-1$. Here $\pi$ sends the closed point of $L$ to $t$, and $\pi(j(v'))=\pi(\varphi(v'))=\pi(v)$ is the original general point; this is precisely the required equation on $T$. The specialization was arbitrary, proving the converse; the final pullback assertion is the forward direction.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NS-89d0cdfe5 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item. The statement is unchanged and matches ILO XIV Def. 2.1.1/Prop. 2.1.3 (printed pp.209-210; immediate means the closure in X_(ybar) has dimension 1) and Def. 2.1.8 with the paragraph after it (pp.211-212; delta(special)=delta(general)-1, etale restriction), as used at the strict-local opening of Prop. 2.5.4 (p.217). I tested it on a field, the empty scheme, a trait, nilpotents and a larger Omega. The direction (<=) holds because immediate geometric specializations are defined inside strict localizations. Step 1 is correct: pi factors through an affine U containing t (local-spectrum argument), the chart lemma applies (Omega algebraically closed, e=id), so the ind-etale invariance hypothesis holds on all of L, and functoriality (1) gives the closed lift c. Step 2 is correct: invariance at b gives L_(b) iso T_(pi b) over T, which carries the closure and the closed point. Step 3 is correct, but it said the closed-point iteration gives an isomorphism L_(c)->L 'over L'. The cited invariance statement (its proof step 5 confirms) only gives the canonical phi: L_(c)->T_(tbar)=L over T, and the step also mixed v with its lift (C3/C4 imprecision). FIX: Step 3 is rewritten with v'=phi^{-1}(v) and pi(j v')=pi(phi v')=pi(v). Step 2 now cites functoriality clause (1) for the closed-point images, which is added to its uses. There are no new nodes.
